sourcePolicy: Published original treatments and dated official/curated secondary biodiversity sources retain distinct source types; no inferred local occurrence or invented conservation status.

items.label: Carapace and build
items.statement: Broad, flattened, heavily reinforced shell; adults can exceed 30 cm carapace length.
items.source: Diesmos et al. (2012), Chelonian Research Monographs 5, account 066
items.scopeLimit: Published Palawan populations and the 2012 account; old Leyte type locality was erroneous.

items.label: Palawan riparian forest
items.statement: Published habitat includes northern Palawan's lowland forests along creeks and rivers.
items.source: Diesmos et al. (2012), Chelonian Research Monographs 5, account 066
items.scopeLimit: Published Palawan populations and the 2012 account; old Leyte type locality was erroneous.

items.label: Corrected island occurrence
items.statement: The 2012 account documents populations in Palawan and identifies the old Leyte type locality as erroneous.
items.source: Diesmos et al. (2012), Chelonian Research Monographs 5, account 066
items.scopeLimit: Published Palawan populations and the 2012 account; old Leyte type locality was erroneous.

items.label: Clutch size
items.statement: Known clutches contain one or two eggs; the account reports mean egg dimensions around 49.6 × 26.5 mm.
items.source: Diesmos et al. (2012), Chelonian Research Monographs 5, account 066
items.scopeLimit: Published Palawan populations and the 2012 account; old Leyte type locality was erroneous.

items.label: Historical Red List category
items.statement: The 2012 account reports Critically Endangered from an IUCN assessment dated 2000.
items.source: Diesmos et al. (2012), Chelonian Research Monographs 5, account 066
items.scopeLimit: Published Palawan populations and the 2012 account; old Leyte type locality was erroneous.

items.label: Large softshell body
items.statement: A large, low-bodied softshell turtle; the 2008 species account reports adult carapaces commonly within 60–100 cm.
items.source: Das (2008), Chelonian Research Monographs 5, account 011
items.scopeLimit: Broad Asian species complex. Philippine population identity may change under future taxonomic revision.

items.label: Rivers to estuaries
items.statement: Recorded in rivers, lakes, estuaries and occasionally shallow coastal marine habitats.
items.source: Das (2008), Chelonian Research Monographs 5, account 011
items.scopeLimit: Broad Asian species complex. Philippine population identity may change under future taxonomic revision.

items.label: 2018 global assessment
items.statement: The global IUCN assessment dated 1 July 2018, published in 2021, lists Critically Endangered, A2cd+4cd.
items.source: Choudhury et al. (2021), IUCN Red List: Pelochelys cantorii
items.scopeLimit: Global status assessed 1 July 2018, published 2021, separate from Philippine national listing.

items.label: Population direction
items.statement: The 2018 IUCN global assessment reports a decreasing population trend.
items.source: Choudhury et al. (2021), IUCN Red List: Pelochelys cantorii
items.scopeLimit: Global status assessed 1 July 2018, published 2021, separate from Philippine national listing.

items.label: Pale northern cloud rat
items.statement: Northern/central Luzon cloud rats are commonly pale or nearly white with dark ears, tail and a dark facial mask.
items.source: Field Museum, Slender-tailed Cloud Rats, Philippine Mammals project
items.scopeLimit: Museum project species description, not a newly dated peer-reviewed field study.

items.label: Forest leaves
items.statement: The museum account describes tender leaves as a main food for slender-tailed cloud rats.
items.source: Field Museum, Slender-tailed Cloud Rats, Philippine Mammals project
items.scopeLimit: Museum project species description, not a newly dated peer-reviewed field study.

items.label: Greater Luzon region
items.statement: The ASM database places the species in the northern and central Luzon faunal region.
items.source: ASM Mammal Diversity Database, Phloeomys pallidus, v2.5
items.scopeLimit: Curated mammal reference. Range is regional, not a proof of occurrence at a particular survey station.

items.label: Dark southern cloud rat
items.statement: The southern Luzon giant cloud rat usually has a deep mahogany-brown coat.
items.source: Field Museum, Slender-tailed Cloud Rats, Philippine Mammals project
items.scopeLimit: Museum project species description, not a newly dated peer-reviewed field study.

items.label: Tree browsing
items.statement: The museum account describes cloud rats browsing tender young leaves in forest trees.
items.source: Field Museum, Slender-tailed Cloud Rats, Philippine Mammals project
items.scopeLimit: Museum project species description, not a newly dated peer-reviewed field study.

items.label: Original genus and name
items.statement: The ASM MDD traces the original 1839 name to Mus (Phloeomys) Cumingi.
items.source: ASM Mammal Diversity Database, Phloeomys cumingi, v2.5
items.sourceLocation: Taxonomy, original name and type locality
items.scopeLimit: Curated MDD taxonomy record; not a new field-survey publication.

items.label: Arboreal forest habitat
items.statement: AMNH summarizes the species in arboreal microhabitats of primary forests on Negros and Panay.
items.source: AMNH Amphibian Species of the World, Platymantis negrosensis (1997 original description cited)
items.scopeLimit: Original source is Brown et al. 1997; the web account is curated secondary literature.

items.label: Negros and Panay mountains
items.statement: The AMNH account reports Negros and Panay island populations at roughly 200–1,800 m.
items.source: AMNH Amphibian Species of the World, Platymantis negrosensis (1997 original description cited)
items.scopeLimit: Original source is Brown et al. 1997; the web account is curated secondary literature.

items.label: Negros and Masbate mountains
items.statement: The AMNH taxonomic account lists mountains on Negros and Masbate at roughly 600–1,700 m.
items.source: AMNH Amphibian Species of the World, Platymantis hazelae (Taylor 1920)
items.sourceLocation: Original type locality; current distribution; synonym discussion
items.scopeLimit: 1920 original type area and currently summarized island records; not a diagnostic morphology study.

items.label: 1920 original name
items.statement: Taylor first described this taxon as Philautus hazelae from Mt. Canlaon, Negros.
items.source: AMNH Amphibian Species of the World, Platymantis hazelae (Taylor 1920)
items.sourceLocation: Original type locality; current distribution; synonym discussion
items.scopeLimit: 1920 original type area and currently summarized island records; not a diagnostic morphology study.

items.label: Banahao massif
items.statement: The published original-description locality is Mt. Banahao, Quezon, Luzon, near 1,100 m elevation.
items.source: AMNH Amphibian Species of the World, Platymantis banahao (Brown et al. 1997)
items.sourceLocation: Original type locality and current range
items.scopeLimit: Reference to the original published description, not a specimen-level identification key.

items.label: 1997 described taxon
items.statement: Brown and colleagues described P. banahao in the 1997 revision of the guentheri group.
items.source: AMNH Amphibian Species of the World, Platymantis banahao (Brown et al. 1997)
items.sourceLocation: Original type locality and current range
